text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Mutual pleasure and positive results from Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal's visit to Jordan yesterday.
- Ministry of Supply studies issuing subsidy coupons instead of financial support to Jordan's poor.

- Parliamentary speaker condemns Moslem Brotherhood comments that opposition should seek support from democratic movements and human rights groups in the United States to help topple the government's amendments to press and publications law.
- Trial of Ahmed al-Daqamsa continues with testimony from four prosecution witnesses.
AL-DUSTOUR
- Director General of Social Security organisation says changes in social security to be discussed next month.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali calls for Saudi market to open up to Jordanian goods. Prince Saud says Saudi Arabia supports Jordan and would not let any crisis befall it.

- Cabinet approves the sale by Housing Bank of half of the Forte Grand hotel to an Arab investment body. Two parties agree to set up joint company to own the hotel called Housing Company for Tourism and Hotel Investments.
- Housing Bank shares to be issued at five dinars each as part of capital increase.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- Fist fight in court between Daqamsa and security men.
- Crisis between minstry of industry and energy and National Cable company over tender for supply of cable linking Jordan and Syria.
AL-ASWAQ
- Tribal allegiance will be strongest weapon in parliamentary elections, opinion poll finds.
- International Silica Company set up with capitalisation of 1.5 million dinars ($2.1 million).
JORDAN TIMES
- Crown Prince Hassan and Saud al-Faisal discuss peace, means to cement bilateral relations.
- Another public holiday next week -- Army Day on June 10.
- Jordanians rate democracy at middle of road, losing faith in press, according to poll.
